subject: docs/coop/artifacts/state-class-contract.v1.json

blockers.title: The purported closed preview-byte placement omits named durable preview state.
evidence: purpose claims to assign or reserve every named durable byte the preview actually writes, but bytePlacement has only six entries and contains no entry or reservation for the monotonic trust store: trust roots, revocation observations, expiry floors, and anti-rollback counters.

Live file 04 lines 78-79 require those values to be separate monotonic state that never rolls back with executable pointers. D-002 includes DR-112 in the slice-affected row set and scopes G08 to the root/index/core/component install-trust surfaces the preview ships, so this is not a deferred authoritative-evidence store.

The live DR-G19 row requires every durable/rebuildable state byte to have one declared class, owner, writer, and lifecycle. As corroboration, signed-index-trust-contract.v8 at fc171321e969c74464dbc9ff67edd9b874aac1d1c7375c7dc8e431469442efe0 consumes this exact subject digest yet still records monotonic-store encoding/state-class assignment as riding DR-107/DR-124 and remaining unassigned; D-105 records that v8 as DR-112's accepted design-contract candidate while leaving DR-112 OPEN.

File 04 also says local purge is audited and journaled, and D-002 routes the slice's local purge through DR-124/DR-114/DR-G12/DR-107. bytePlacement names neither a purge journal nor a reservation for it; 'lock / lease / generation journal' does not identify the separately named purge record.
blockers.impact: The candidate can be recorded as though it closes the preview inventory while two implementations lawfully choose different classes, owners, writers, Plan/Run consequences, backup/purge behavior, or migration rules for the omitted trust and purge bytes. That falsifies the artifact's exhaustive purpose and leaves the core DR-G19 invariant untestable.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add a closed census entry for every named preview durable/rebuildable store, at minimum the monotonic trust/revocation/expiry/anti-rollback store and the local purge journal. For each, either assign exactly one class with its owner, writer, and inherited/overriding lifecycle made explicit, or reserve it to a named unresolved owner without claiming the preview inventory closed. Reconcile the resulting declarations with DR-112, DR-107, DR-G12, and DR-G19 without designing authoritative-evidence recipes or minting a purge/D9 result code.

conclusion: REJECT. The prompt's six named attack classes are otherwise clean, but SCC-V1-B1 defeats the candidate's exhaustive byte-placement claim and leaves DR-G19's one-class/owner/writer/lifecycle invariant open. This review does not apply the candidate, change DR-124, claim SATISFIED or QUALIFIED, or authorize implementation.
